metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.taskDescription: Write a lab report investigating the effect of temperature on catalase activity in potato tissue, including hypothesis, method, results and evaluation.

overview.assignmentPurpose: To assess students' ability to design, conduct, and analyze a biological experiment while demonstrating scientific reasoning.
overview.submissionFormat: A formal lab report (800-1000 words) with sections: Title, Introduction, Hypothesis, Method, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion.

criteria.name: Knowledge & Understanding
criteria.criterionIntent: Evaluates student understanding of enzyme principles, experimental design, and biological concepts related to the investigation.

advanced.description: Demonstrates exceptional understanding of enzyme function, active sites, and denaturation. Explains the relationship between temperature and enzyme activity with detailed biological reasoning. Shows thorough understanding of experimental design principles, including controls and variables. Discusses findings in the context of broader biological concepts and theories.
advanced.feedback: Excellent grasp of enzyme biology. Your explanations are thorough and scientifically accurate.

proficient.description: Demonstrates secure understanding of enzyme function and the effect of temperature on activity. Explains denaturation and the concept of optimal temperature clearly. Shows good understanding of experimental design, identifying key variables and controls. Discusses findings with appropriate biological terminology and concepts.
proficient.feedback: Good understanding of enzyme principles. Your explanations are clear and scientifically sound.

basic.description: Demonstrates adequate understanding of basic enzyme function and the effect of temperature on activity. Explains denaturation but with limited detail. Shows some understanding of experimental design but may not fully explain the purpose of all controls or variables. Uses appropriate biological terminology inconsistently.
basic.feedback: Satisfactory understanding of enzyme concepts. Develop explanations with more biological detail.

emerging.description: Demonstrates limited understanding of enzyme function and the effect of temperature. Struggles to explain denaturation or optimal temperature. Shows minimal understanding of experimental design principles. Uses inappropriate or insufficient biological terminology. Explanations are vague or contain misconceptions.
emerging.feedback: Needs to develop understanding of enzyme principles and experimental design fundamentals.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.criterionIntent: Evaluates the precision of measurements, data recording, calculations, and the accuracy of conclusions drawn from the results.

advanced.description: All measurements and data recordings are precise and accurate. Tables and graphs are professionally presented with appropriate scales and units. Calculations are error-free and clearly shown. Conclusions are directly and accurately supported by the data with quantitative evidence. Discusses anomalies with plausible biological explanations.
advanced.feedback: Excellent precision in data collection and analysis. Your results are presented professionally.

proficient.description: Measurements and data recordings are mostly accurate with minor errors. Tables and graphs are well-presented with appropriate scales and units. Calculations are mostly accurate with minor errors. Conclusions are generally supported by the data with some quantitative evidence.
proficient.feedback: Good accuracy in data handling. Ensure all calculations are double-checked.

basic.description: Measurements and data recordings contain several noticeable errors. Tables and graphs are adequately presented but may have minor issues with scaling or units. Calculations contain some errors that affect results. Conclusions are supported by the data but lack sufficient quantitative evidence.
basic.feedback: Improve precision in measurements and calculations. Check your data presentation carefully.

emerging.description: Measurements and data recordings contain significant errors. Tables and graphs are poorly presented with inappropriate scales or missing units. Calculations contain major errors. Conclusions are not well-supported by the data or are inconsistent with findings.
emerging.feedback: Needs significant improvement in data recording and calculation accuracy.

criteria.name: Application
criteria.criterionIntent: Evaluates the student's ability to apply scientific knowledge to plan the investigation, analyze results, and evaluate the method and outcomes.

advanced.description: Method is detailed, logical, and shows excellent planning. Identifies and controls variables effectively. Results are analyzed with sophisticated statistical methods or comparisons. Evaluation is insightful, identifying multiple strengths and weaknesses of the method with detailed suggestions for improvement. Discusses limitations and their impact on results comprehensively.
advanced.feedback: Excellent application of scientific methodology. Your evaluation shows critical thinking and scientific reasoning.

proficient.description: Method is detailed and logical with good planning. Controls variables effectively. Results are analyzed appropriately with clear comparisons. Evaluation identifies several strengths and weaknesses of the method with reasonable suggestions for improvement. Discusses limitations and their impact on results.
proficient.feedback: Good application of scientific methods. Your evaluation is thorough and thoughtful.

basic.description: Method is adequate but lacks some detail in planning. Controls variables but with some omissions. Results are analyzed with basic comparisons. Evaluation identifies some strengths and weaknesses of the method with limited suggestions for improvement. Discusses limitations superficially.
basic.feedback: Satisfactory application of scientific methods. Develop a more detailed evaluation of your procedure.

emerging.description: Method lacks detail and logical planning. Fails to adequately control variables. Results are analyzed with minimal or inappropriate comparisons. Evaluation is superficial, identifying few strengths and weaknesses with no constructive suggestions. Discusses limitations inadequately or not at all.
emerging.feedback: Needs to develop better planning and analytical skills for scientific investigations.

moderationGuidance: Ensure consistent interpretation of 'Knowledge & Understanding' by focusing on the depth of biological explanations rather than report length. Pay particular attention to how students connect temperature effects to enzyme structure and function.

For 'Accuracy', maintain consistency by checking all numerical data against raw measurements. When evaluating graphs, focus on correct scaling, units, and representation of data trends rather than aesthetic qualities.
